### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. complement component 3 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-198933, Reactome:R-HSA-9938027)

**Proposed mechanism:** CD40 (HGNC:2105) —DISRUPTS→ B cell activation and antibody production (GO:0002376); B cell activation and antibody production (GO:0002376) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002719); C3 (HGNC:2105) —DISRUPTS→ Complement system activation (GO:0006955); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002719); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Deficiency in complement component C3 (HP:0004970). Loss of function in CD40 leads to impaired B cell activation and antibody production, resulting in hyper-IgM syndrome and recurrent infections. Loss of function in C3 directly impairs complement system activation, leading to a deficiency in C3 and increased susceptibility to infections.

**How to falsify it:** If a patient with hyper-IgM syndrome type 3 exhibits normal complement component 3 levels and function, and a patient with complement component 3 deficiency exhibits normal CD40 signaling and antibody class switching, this would falsify the proposed overlap. _(variant: A common variant (AF > 1%) in CD40 or C3 associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of immune system dysfunction, specifically involving antibody production and complement activation, can inform therapeutic strategies for recurrent infections in both hyper-IgM syndrome and C3 deficiency, potentially through immune reconstitution or targeted therapies that bolster complement function or antibody responses.

#### 2. obsolete blood group system, landsteiner-wiener  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.361)

Loss-of-function mutations in ICAM4 disrupt integrin signaling, affecting cell adhesion and leading to abnormal blood group phenotypes. The convergence is hypothesized through the shared role of CD40 and ICAM4 in immune cell adhesion and communication pathways which, when disrupted, can manifest in distinct but related immune and cellular dysfunctions.
